title: Multi-modal Siamese Network for Entity Alignment

problem.claim: Multi-modal entity alignment is needed to facilitate integration of multiple multi-modal knowledge graphs from separate data sources.

gap.claim: Prior methods use multi-modal knowledge through heuristic merging of uni-modal feature embeddings, which can largely ignore inter-modal cues.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Multi-modal Siamese Network for Entity Alignment (MSNEA) that leverages inter-modal effects to align entities in different multi-modal knowledge graphs.
MSNEA uses a multi-modal knowledge embedding module to extract visual, relational, and attribute features and generate holistic entity representations.
MSNEA uses inter-modal enhancement mechanisms and a multi-modal contrastive learning module to fuse modalities while reducing the impact of weak modalities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe MSNEA as a novel method for multi-modal entity alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two public datasets are reported to show state-of-the-art performance with a large margin over competitive baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: The growth of multi-modal knowledge graphs creates demand for multi-modal entity alignment.
Existing approaches rely on heuristic merging of uni-modal embeddings and may overlook inter-modal cues.
The paper introduces MSNEA to align entities while comprehensively exploiting inter-modal effects.
The method builds holistic representations, enhances cross-modal feature learning, and applies contrastive fusion to limit weak-modality effects.
The authors report state-of-the-art results on two public datasets against competitive baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method integrates visual, relational, and attribute features while using inter-modal enhancement and contrastive learning.

interpretation.claim: Alignment quality may benefit from modeling interactions among modalities rather than simply merging separate modality embeddings.

application.claim: For multi-modal alignment systems, explicitly model cross-modal guidance and account for modality weakness during fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices generalize beyond the two reported public datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two datasets, baseline identities, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results for the proposed modules.
